evidence_items.summary:
Objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) use and computational approaches have transformed the discovery of plant-derived bioactive chemicals for
cancer treatment. This review synthesized evidence on AI-based approaches, including network pharmacology, molecular docking, and machine
learning, for identifying and validating anticancer plant-derived phytochemicals, focusing on their molecular targets and signaling pathways. Data
Sources: PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched between October 2020 and
July 2025. Study Selection: Studies with at least one AI or computational method, investigating plant-derived phytochemicals for anticancer effects,
reporting quantitative computational outcomes, and offering free full-text access in English were included. Review articles, conference abstracts,
non-plant studies, and non-English publications were excluded. Data Extraction: Two reviewers extracted data on predefined variables. An
adapted PROBAST tool was used to assess risk of bias for in silico studies and modified SYRCLE tools for in vitro and in vivo studies, with
certainty of evidence evaluated using the GRADE method. Data Synthesis: Eighteen studies satisfied the inclusion criteria. The most frequently
discovered bioactive chemical was quercetin, which targets breast cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and lung cancer via AKT1, EGFR, TP53,
and MAPK signaling pathways. The majority of in silico studies have a high risk of bias, while in vitro and in vivo studies were rated as having
some concerns. The overall certainty of evidence was low. Conclusion: AI-based computational techniques have become critical tools for
discovering plant-derived compounds and identifying multi-target mechanisms involving AKT1, EGFR, and PI3K/Akt signaling.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Discovery of Plant-Derived Bioactive Compounds in Cancer Therapeutics: Computational Approaches and Molecular Target Identification

evidence_items.summary: The article analyses theoretical and methodological foundations for developing future teachers’ research competence through artificial intelligence tools within comparative pedagogy. It specifies motivational-axiological, cognitive, operational-research, digital-AI, and ethical-reflexive components of the competence. A methodology is proposed that integrates problem formulation, source search and verification, construction of comparative criteria, evidence synthesis, academic writing, and reflective evaluation. The methodology is grounded in human Ta’limda istiqbolli izlanishlar - xalqaro ilmiy-metodik jurnal № 8/2026 ISSN: 3060-527X 2 oversight, academic integrity, source reliability, and sensitivity to national context. Its potential to strengthen the consistency of comparative analysis and students’ independent researcher stance is substantiated, while AI is treated as a cognitive partner rather than a substitute for scholarly judgement.

evidence_items.summary: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) for electronic contact (e-contact) offers new possibilities for intergroup contact. This pilot study examined whether exchanging instant messages with an AI-generated out-group member reduces prejudice, using explicit and implicit pre- and post-contact evaluations with a pure control condition. The contact was designed in accordance with Allport's optimal contact conditions and strategies derived from categorization theories. Sixty-one Japanese adults participated in this study. One month after the pre-evaluation, participants in the contact condition engaged in a 15-min interaction with a text-based AI designed to represent a Chinese individual, during which they introduced themselves and discussed possible joint efforts toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. The results showed that the contact condition increased explicit measures of positive attitudes and intergroup empathy while reducing negative attitudes relative to the control condition. However, intergroup anxiety and implicit attitudes measured using the Implicit Association Test showed no contact effects. Our findings suggest that a brief, semi-structured contact involving personalized interaction and cooperation task may mitigate some aspects of explicit intergroup bias. This preliminary evidence indicates new possibilities for applying conversational AI in instant messaging environments within intergroup contexts and provides implications for effective e-contact strategies.
evidence_items.title: Text-messaging with a conversational AI as an out-group member: Preliminary evidence for a new application of intergroup contact.

evidence_items.summary:
Purpose: This study presents an original test of whether generative artificial intelligence (AI) can detect the internal conceptual coherence within a set of papers produced over several years. The analysis is based on five papers on innovation in the insurance sector, evaluated using M365 Copilot (GPT-5 model).

Methodology/approach: The full texts of five conference papers, co-authored by the author of this study, were provided to the AI tool, and it was asked to reconstruct the conceptual development and main research direction across them.

Findings: The AI tool identified both the chronological order and thematic development of the articles, showing a consistent progression from general reflections on risk toward a more structured, taxonomic model. However, result quality depends strongly on prompt clarity and user experience.

Research limitations/implications: The small, specific sample limits generalisability, and the analysis is bound by the content provided and the model's current capabilities. AI can support self-assessment and exploration of research development but should not replace peer review or formal evaluation.

Originality/value: A literature check conducted by the tool suggests that this use of AI to analyse long-term conceptual coherence in an author's work is relatively new. The study contributes to the literature on AI in research methodology by applying AI to assess the development of a research agenda over time, rather than single publications. It shows that LLMs can connect dispersed ideas, highlight practical implications, and suggest future research directions, offering a useful tool for researchers reviewing the evolution of their own work.
evidence_items.title: AI-based diagnosis of the continuity of research thought: A case study from the perspective of innovation and management accounting

evidence_items.summary:
Purpose: The aim of the paper is to identify patterns of teaching recommendations generated by generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in relation to the design of accounting education in higher education.

Methodology/approach: The study employs a qualitative research approach based on an analysis of responses generated by the ChatGPT language model to a set of structured prompts concerning instructional design. The analysis covered nine accounting courses. The empirical material was coded and analysed using qualitative content analysis supported by MAXQDA software.

Findings: The results indicate that the recommendations generated by the model most frequently concern student-active teaching methods, particularly teamwork, case analysis, and moderated discussion. In terms of assessment, the model’s recommendations most frequently point to evaluation methods that allow for the verification of students’ reasoning, such as open-ended questions and tasks requiring justification of answers. AI is primarily presented as a tool to support analysis and reflection rather than replacing students’ cognitive activity.

Research limitations/implications: The study is exploratory and based on AI-generated content; therefore, the findings do not constitute an empirical evaluation of the effectiveness of the proposed teaching methods.

Originality/value: The paper contributes to the literature on generative AI in higher education by identifying patterns of AI-generated teaching recommendations and interpreting them within the context of learning theories, understood as a set of concepts that explain the mechanisms of knowledge acquisition, as well as the roles of the learner and the teacher in the educational process.
evidence_items.title: Patterns of AI-generated teaching recommendations in accounting education: A qualitative analysis of ChatGPT responses

evidence_items.summary: Cross-reference simulation combines multiple simulation codes when one code requires data produced by another. To provide an efficient and convenient solution for cross-reference Solar-Terrestrial Physics (STP) simulation, a framework called Code-To-Code Adapter (CoToCoA) Library has been developed. CoToCoA was designed to implement cross-reference simulation with minimal modifications to the simulation codes while maintaining low overhead and currently supports only C and Fortran. To further enhance its usability by integrating CoToCoA with Python, we developed a Python interface. Two development approaches were conducted: (1) direct development of CoToCoA in Python and (2) the use of a library to call C functions of CoToCoA from Python. To evaluate the performance of the Python interfaces, experiments of data transfer methods in CoToCoA were performed. As a result of the evaluation, the library-based implementation showed performance comparable to the native C implementation, while the direct implementation required more additional time. The results show that the Python interface using the library enables efficient data transfer from both C- and Fortran-based STP simulation programs to Python for advanced data analysis and processing. Furthermore, the developed Python interface was applied to low-latency online visualization of magnetohydrodynamics simulation results. The framework has the potential of extension to integration with other Python tools, such as machine-learning or artificial intelligence models.
evidence_items.title: Development of a python interface for a framework of cross-reference solar-terrestrial physics simulation

evidence_items.summary: Fragility fractures represent a significant global health burden, with osteoporosis affecting over 500 million individuals and contributing to nearly 9 million fractures annually. Conventional diagnosis relies on dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) to measure bone mineral density (BMD), yet BMD alone explains only part of fracture risk. Many fractures occur in patients without osteoporosis by DEXA criteria, underscoring the limitations of bone quantity-based assessment. Advances in imaging and biomarker research highlight the importance of bone quality, microarchitecture, and marrow composition in fracture prediction. Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques - including T1ρ, T2 mapping, proton density fat fraction, and diffusion-weighted imaging - offer non-invasive insights into collagen integrity, proteoglycan content, water distribution, and marrow adiposity. These parameters correlate with trabecular deterioration and cortical porosity, enhancing risk stratification beyond BMD. Similarly, Vertebral Bone Quality (VBQ) scoring, derived from routine T1-weighted MRI, provides a practical surrogate for bone quality by quantifying vertebral marrow signal intensity relative to cerebrospinal fluid. Modified VBQ improves accuracy by minimising posterior vertebral artefacts, demonstrating stronger correlation with DEXA T scores and trabecular microarchitecture. Studies show VBQ predicts vertebral fragility fractures independently of BMD, with sensitivity exceeding 90% and discriminatory ability comparable to the fracture risk assessment tool and trabecular bone score. Integration of quantitative MRI and VBQ/modified VBQ into predictive models, supported by artificial intelligence, enables opportunistic, radiation-free screening and more precise fracture risk assessment. Together, these advanced imaging biomarkers represent a paradigm shift toward comprehensive evaluation of bone strength, bridging the gap between bone quantity and quality for improved prevention and management of fragility fractures.
evidence_items.title: Fragility fracture risk prediction using quantitative magnetic resonance and Vertebral Bone Quality scoring beyond density

evidence_items.summary: Small-fiber neuropathy is a common complication of metabolic, neurodegenerative, and treatment-related disorders. Early detection can be challenging because established diagnostic approaches may be invasive, resource-intensive, or relatively insensitive to early small-fiber injury. Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) is a rapid, noninvasive imaging technique that enables quantitative assessment of the corneal subbasal nerve plexus and has been proposed as a biomarker of peripheral small-fiber damage. This minireview critically evaluates the role of CCM for early detection, diagnostic testing, prognostic stratification, longitudinal follow-up, and treatment response assessment in systemic neuropathies, particularly diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). Evidence is strongest in DPN, in which CCM consistently demonstrates group-level corneal nerve loss; however, individual diagnostic performance is only moderate and varies according to patient spectrum, reference standard, sampling protocol, analysis method, and diagnostic threshold. Evidence in other neurologic diseases, including Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, is less robust. Advancements in automated image analysis and artificial intelligence have improved reproducibility and efficiency of corneal nerve quantification in recent years. Nevertheless, widespread implementation in the clinics is still hampered by methodological heterogeneity, lack of full standardization, and absence of universally validated diagnostic and prognostic cut-off points. CCM is therefore a promising tool for translational research and precision medicine, but population-level differences in corneal nerve parameters should not be interpreted as establishing an individual diagnosis. At present, CCM should complement rather than replace established clinical, neurophysiological, functional, and pathological assessments, including quantitative sensory testing and skin biopsy when clinically indicated. Before integration into clinical practice can be recommended, multi-center prospective studies utilizing standardized acquisition and analysis protocols, validated thresholds, and clinically meaningful patient outcomes are required.
evidence_items.title: Corneal nerve imaging in systemic neuropathy: A minireview of experimental and precision medicine applications

evidence_items.summary: Global supply chains that support internationally traded goods and industrial services have become increasingly vulnerable to disruptions arising from geopolitical conflicts, economic uncertainty, climate-related disasters, cybersecurity threats, and transportation bottlenecks. These disruptions have exposed the limitations of conventional risk management approaches and created a growing need for quantitative methods capable of predicting uncertainty and supporting evidence-based decision making. Probability theory offers a rigorous analytical framework for assessing disruption likelihoods and improving supply chain resilience. This study investigates the application of probability theory in assessing and mitigating risks across global supply chains for internationally traded goods and services. A mixed-methods research design was employed, integrating Monte Carlo simulation, Bayesian networks, chi-square testing, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis to evaluate major supply chain risk factors and their operational impacts. The findings indicate that supply chain disruptions are not evenly distributed across regions, with North America and Europe experiencing the highest disruption frequencies, confirmed by the Chi-square test (χ² = 43.27, p < 0.01). Monte Carlo simulation showed that high-risk disruption events occur with probabilities ranging from 20% to 60%. Multiple regression analysis identified geopolitical risks (β = 1.50), economic downturns (β = 1.20), and supply chain congestion (β = 1.80) as the strongest predictors of supply chain disruptions (R² = 0.78, p < 0.001). Pearson correlation analysis further demonstrated a strong positive relationship between disruption frequency and economic losses (r = 0.85, p < 0.001). The study concludes that integrating probability-based analytical models significantly improves risk prediction, decision quality, and supply chain resilience. It recommends the adoption of real-time data analytics, artificial intelligence-driven forecasting, digital technologies, and collaborative risk-sharing mechanisms to strengthen the resilience of global supply chains for internationally traded goods and services.
evidence_items.title: Using Probability Theory to Assess and Mitigate Risks in Global Supply Chains for Internationally Traded Goods and Services

evidence_items.summary: Insufficient physical activity remains a major public health concern among young adults and many university students fail to meet recommended activity levels. This study aimed to quantify the contributions of university sports programs to achieving physical activity recommendations and to examine differences according to sport categories and gender among university students. A total of 593 students from Heidelberg University participated (mean age = 23.44 years, SD = 4.66), with valid step count data from 531 and MET data from 513 participants. Physical activity was objectively measured during sports sessions using a multi-sensor device. The university sports programs, which largely follow a traditional classification by type of sport, were divided into six categories. Descriptive statistics were used to assess contributions to daily physical activity benchmarks, and two-way ANOVAs examined main effects of sport category and gender on step counts and MET as well as interaction effects. On average, participants accumulated 3134 steps (SD = 1303) per session, corresponding to approximately 44.77% of a 7000-step benchmark. Mean activity intensity was 3.58 MET (SD = 1.07), indicating predominantly moderate-intensity activity. Sport category showed significant effects on both step counts (ηp² = 0.26) and MET (ηp² = 0.18), with team sports associated with the highest values. Gender differences were small but significant for MET (η² = 0.01), with higher values observed in male participants, while no main effect was found for step counts. Significant interaction effects indicated that gender differences varied by sport category. University sports programs contribute substantially to students’ physical activity through both step accumulation and moderate-intensity exercise. Their effectiveness varies by sport category, with team sports showing the highest activity levels. Gender differences were small and context-dependent, suggesting that activity levels are shaped by interactions between individual and activity-specific factors. These findings highlight the role of university sports as a key component of health-promoting university settings and emphasize the need for accessible opportunities that support broad student participation in regular physical activity.
evidence_items.title: University sports programs as a health promoting setting contribute to physical activity recommendations with differences across sport categories and gender at Heidelberg University, Germany

evidence_items.summary: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance has intensified the search for new bioactive compounds from natural sources. This study investigated the chemical composition and antimicrobial activity of the essential oil (EO) extracted from the leaves of Vepris salicifolia (Engl.) Mziray. In addition, the molecular interactions and drug-like properties of δ-cadinene, the major constituent of the EO, were evaluated. The EO was extracted by hydrodistillation and subsequently characterized chemically using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). The antibacterial and antifungal activities of the EO and δ-cadinene were assessed using disc diffusion and agar dilution assays, while molecular docking and ADMET analyses were performed to elucidate the potential mechanism of antimicrobial action and evaluate the pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness properties of δ-cadinene. GC–MS analysis identified 26 compounds, representing 84.3% of the EO. The predominant constituents were δ-cadinene (23.5%), intermedeol (18.3%), germacrene D (10.2%), α-muurolol (9.0%), and germacrene D-4-ol (7.5%). The EO and δ-cadinene effectively inhibited the growth of a wide range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and fungi. Notably, δ-cadinene showed antibacterial activity against S. aureus ML267, with an inhibition zone of 17.8 mm, comparable to that of ciprofloxacin (18.0 mm). Furthermore, the EO exhibited greater antifungal activity against Penicillium notatum, with an inhibition zone of 14.0 mm compared with 11.0 mm for griseofulvin. Docking results showed favorable binding energies for δ-cadinene with the CrtM enzyme of S. aureus (− 7.757 kcal/mol) and the CYP51 enzyme of P. notatum (− 5.756 kcal/mol). ADMET studies further revealed that δ-cadinene has favorable drug-like characteristics, including high intestinal permeability and oral bioavailability, and did not predict any cardiotoxicity. The findings of this study indicate that V. salicifolia leaf EO, particularly δ-cadinene, represents a promising source of antimicrobial agents for future medicinal applications. Nevertheless, the predicted molecular mechanisms of δ-cadinene should be validated through enzyme inhibition assays.
evidence_items.title: Antimicrobial activity of Vepris salicifolia leaf essential oil and δ-cadinene: in vitro evaluation and in silico mechanistic insights into δ-cadinene

evidence_items.summary: Dental caries is a microbiome-driven disease in which acidogenic taxa dominated by Streptococcus mutans displace commensal genera and form a glucan-rich biofilm matrix that demineralises enamel. Chlorhexidine (CHX) is the standard chemical adjunct but causes staining, dysgeusia and broad commensal suppression, motivating evaluation of botanical alternatives that may rebalance the oral ecosystem. This study determined the antibiofilm and microbiome-modulatory effects of standardised Indonesian Syzygium aromaticum L. (clove, Myrtaceae) bud essential oil (SAEO) on saliva-derived polymicrobial cariogenic biofilms in vitro. SAEO was hydrodistilled, characterised by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, and tested at 0.25%, 0.5% and 1.0% v/v against polymicrobial biofilms grown on hydroxyapatite discs from stimulated saliva of 60 caries-active adults; 0.12% CHX was the positive control (n = 6 biological replicates per arm). Endpoints were biofilm biomass, CFU on selective media, EPS, biofilm pH, lactate, 16S rRNA microbiome profiling and HGF-1 cytotoxicity. Eugenol (82.3%), β-caryophyllene (7.4%) and eugenyl acetate (4.8%) were the principal volatiles. SAEO 1.0% reduced biofilm biomass by 70.5% (95% CI 65.8–75.3; p < 0.001), S. mutans CFU by 3.22 log₁₀ and EPS by 67.9%, while raising Shannon diversity from 1.42 to 2.08 bits and restoring Neisseria and Corynebacterium relative abundance — a dysbiosis-reversal pattern absent under CHX. Cytotoxicity remained below 18% at 1.0% v/v versus 31.8% for CHX. Standardised SAEO is a credible complementary anticaries agent meriting clinical translation. Keywords: Syzygium aromaticum; clove essential oil; eugenol; oral microbiome; dental caries; antibiofilm.
evidence_items.title: Antibiofilm and Microbiome-Modulatory Effects of Syzygium aromaticum Essential Oil in an In Vitro Dental Caries Polymicrobial Model

evidence_items.summary: Allelopathy from invasive and medicinal weeds can affect crop establishment, yet species- and concentration-specific impacts on rice remain poorly quantified. This study evaluated the concentration-dependent allelopathic effects of aqueous leaf extracts of Vernonia amygdalina Delile and Chromolaena odorata (L.) R.M. King and H. Rob. on germination and early seedling growth of Jamila rice (Oryza sativa L.). A completely randomised design with five replicates was used. Four concentrations of fresh leaf aqueous extracts were tested for each species: 0% (control), 25%, 50%, and 100% w/v. Radicle and plumule lengths were measured every 3 days for 21 days. One-way ANOVA analysed data and means separated using Duncan’s Multiple Range Test at p ≤ 0.05. C. odorata caused a linear, concentration-dependent inhibition of both radicle and plumule growth. At 21 DAP, 100% C. odorata reduced radicle length by 34% and plumule length by 12% relative to the control (p ≤ 0.05). V. amygdalina exhibited a biphasic hormetic response. The 25% extract stimulated radicle growth by 18% and plumule growth by 5% compared to the control at 21 DAP, while the 100% extract caused 31% inhibition of radicle and 12% inhibition of plumule at 2 DAP (p ≤ 0.05). Inhibitory effects were most pronounced during early ontogeny (2–11 DAP) and became transient by 21 DAP. Both extracts are concentration-dependent modulators of rice seedling growth. C. odorata is consistently inhibitory, while V. amygdalina can be stimulatory at low concentrations and inhibitory at high concentrations. These findings suggest potential for low-dose V. amygdalina as a bio-stimulant and high-dose extracts of both species as natural herbicides, pending field validation. Comparative allelopathic assessment: Investigated and compared the concentration-dependent allelochemics impact of fresh leaf aqueous extracts from Vernonia amygdalina (bitter leaf) and Chromolaena odorata (Siam weed) on the germination dynamics of Jamila rice (Oryza sativa). Biphasic (Hormetic) Response of V. amygdalina: Discovered that V. amygdalina exhibits a dual agronomic nature; lower concentrations (25% w/v) significantly stimulated radicle and plumule elongation, whereas high concentrations (100% w/v) exerted severe phytotoxic inhibition (V0 > V{50%} > V{100%}). Linear Inhibition by C. odorata: Demonstrated that C. odorata extracts cause a strictly linear, concentration-dependent suppression of early seedling growth parameters, following a distinct statutory decline pattern (C0 > C{25%} > C{50%} > C{100%}) for both radicle and plumule development. Transient chronological effects: Revealed that the allelopathic inhibitory stresses of both botanical extracts are highly prominent during early ontogeny (2 to 11 days after planting) but gradually exhibit a transient nature, showing no statistically significant growth differences (p ≥ 0.05) by the conclusion of the 21-day bioassay. Agricultural application insight: Highlights the critical threshold dynamics required when harnessing these bioactive weeds as sustainable biofertilizers or botanical pest-control agents without risking autotoxic or non-target crop suppression in rice-cropping systems.
evidence_items.title: Allelochemics impacts of leaf extracts from Vernonia amygdalina and Chromolaena odorata on germination of rice

evidence_items.summary: Exosomes have emerged as promising cell-free therapeutic agents for tissue regeneration. However, chronic inflammation, a hallmark of periodontal disease, may impair their osteogenic potential. This systematic review evaluated how inflammatory conditions influence the ability of exosomes to modulate osteogenesis in human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSC) in vitro. Electronic databases and grey literature were searched up to February 2026, and study selection followed a two-phase screening process. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias in Dental Preclinical Research Tool (RobDMAT), while certainty of evidence was evaluated using adapted GRADE criteria. Primary outcomes included alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and extracellular matrix mineralization. Due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, a meta-analysis was not performed, and findings were synthesized qualitatively using fold-change comparisons. Six studies were included. Exosome-based interventions consistently enhanced osteogenic outcomes under inflammatory conditions, although with variable magnitude. Extracellular matrix mineralization showed robust increases (> 4-fold) in two studies (10.67- and 4.38-fold), moderate enhancement in one study (3.06-fold), and weak increases (< 2-fold) in three studies (1.95-, 1.60-, and 1.41-fold). ALP activity demonstrated predominantly moderate (3.04-, 3.30-, and 3.83-fold) to robust enhancement (5.50- and 6.75-fold). Limited evidence also suggested a reduction in pro-inflammatory mediators, although this outcome remains insufficiently explored. Exosomes appear to partially overcome the inhibitory effects of inflammation on osteogenesis in hPDLSC, supporting their potential as modulators of regenerative responses in inflammatory microenvironments. Nevertheless, the limited number of studies and methodological heterogeneity restrict the strength of current evidence.
evidence_items.title: Exosome-mediated modulation of osteogenesis under inflammatory conditions: a systematic review of in vitro studies on human periodontal ligament stem cells.

evidence_items.summary: Single-image 3D object generation can now produce high-fidelity assets, yet accurately placing them into a coherent scene layout remains an open challenge. A central difficulty lies in how object layout is represented. Holistic methods absorb placement into a scene-level generation process, sacrificing object-level detail. Compositional methods preserve object fidelity by decoupling geometry from layout, but typically parameterize layout as sparse, unbounded pose variables that are difficult to learn and generalize poorly under scarce scene-level supervision.We present Mira-Scene, a compositional 3D scene reconstruction framework that replaces sparse pose regression with dense, bounded correspondence recovery. At its core is the Canonical Coordinate Map (CCM), a pixel-aligned field that maps each visible object pixel to a surface coordinate in the object's bounded canonical space. When paired with a scene-space Point Cloud Map (PCM) from monocular geometry estimation, CCM induces dense canonical-to-scene correspondences from which object transformations are recovered through robust geometric alignment. Because CCM operates in bounded canonical space, it provides a stable prediction target that can be trained from scalable object-level 3D data without requiring scene-level layout annotations. Mira-Scene further introduces a multimodal diffusion transformer that jointly generates object geometry and CCMs, using modality-specific expert streams with shared attention and positional encoding to promote geometry-layout consistency. Experiments on indoor, outdoor, synthetic, and in-the-wild scenes show that Mira-Scene substantially outperforms strong baselines in layout accuracy, achieving relative gains of 39.8% in 3D-IoU and 16.5% in 2D-IoU over SAM3D, using limited open-source training data.
evidence_items.title: Mira-Scene: Pixel-Aligned Layouts for Generative 3D Scene
